correctness_confidence.basis: I re-derived by hand: the Cesaro test identity |1-a v_j|<=1 when a=2*eta (Prop. 6), the local estimate in Lemma 5, the parameter arithmetic for (1) and (2), P'_{m,k}(0)=n/2+1/4, D(a,c), T(a,c) and the moment identity (19), the cubic (18) for Theorem 11. All checked out. Not checked: the Mathieu uniformity in Thm 3, the outer-arc estimates and implicit-function steps of Thm 2 and 11, which are only sketched. I executed no code.

rigor.basis: The lower bound (Lemmas 4-5, Prop. 6, Thm 1) is explicit and essentially complete. Theorem 3 (uniform Mathieu expansion over lambda) and the upper bounds of Thm 2 and 11 rely on phrases such as 'uniformly bounded', 'eventually', 'by compactness' without explicit constants; Lemma 10 is existence-only.

novelty.basis: Removes the log n factor in exponent of the Tan-Wang-Huang-Chen bound (the abstract of arXiv:2608.02043 confirmed by me via fetch: exp(-(1+o(1)) sqrt(n) log n)) and allows arbitrary slope. The 1/sqrt8 limit via Mathieu and the interior-zero collapse appear new to me but I only did one targeted fetch, not a full literature search; no priority is established.

significance.basis: Narrow, specialized problem (residual of P'-lambda P for Schur-stable polynomials, linked to Erdos Problem 973 already resolved negatively). The sharp zero-count threshold (zero vs one interior zero) is a neat structural statement; the exponent gap between sqrt(n) lower and n^-A upper bounds remains open.

reproducibility.basis: Explicit constants and parameter choices make Theorem 1 checkable. Supplementary diagnostics are mentioned but not part of the PDF, so I could not inspect them; Theorems 2 and 11 give no effective constants.

summary: The manuscript proves (i) for circle-root polynomials, lim s_n = lim r_n = 1/sqrt8 via the Mathieu ground state; (ii) a stretched-exponential lower bound exp(-C sqrt n) for all disk-root polynomials with arbitrary complex slope for C > sqrt((8/3) log 17), explicit exp(-3 sqrt n) for n >= 10^4, improving a cited arXiv result by removing log n; (iii) superalgebraic upper bounds with a fixed number of interior zeros, and collapse n^{-1/6} with exactly one interior zero; (iv) a polynomial barrier if the root radius is fixed. The core lower bound is clean and my hand re-derivation of its steps and constants found no error. The upper-bound constructions are plausible, and the identities I checked are right, but they are argued at sketch level. Abstract claims match the stated theorems and limitations are honestly stated. The result is a solid specialized improvement, not field-shaping.
strengths: Explicit, checkable finite certificate (Prop. 6) with a clever Cesaro test making |1-a v_j|<=1 exact.
Clear honest scoping: no claim of optimal rates, no claim on Erdos 973 yes/no beyond the earlier known answer, AI assistance and absence of human review disclosed.
Sharp dichotomy between zero and one interior zero, with the identities (18)-(19) correct on my check.
weaknesses: Proofs of Theorems 2, 3 (upper/lower uniformity) and 11 are compressed; key uniform estimates are asserted rather than proved.
Lemma 10 and Theorem 2 are non-effective: no bounds on M_A, C_A, N_A.
Large gap between sqrt(n)-stretched-exponential lower bound and the upper bounds; optimal rates unresolved.
Novelty is relative to a very recent, only partially verified literature; the 2020 Komarov related text was not read in full by the author.
potential_errors: Theorem 3: uniform-in-lambda use of the single-variable Mathieu expansion a_0(q) on the window c_n=O(sqrt n); the O(n^-1) remainder is quoted from NIST fixed-index asymptotics and its uniformity is asserted. I did not verify it.
Odd-degree argument that |p| in H^1 has the same quadratic-form values as p and passes to the periodic spectrum: stated briefly, not checked in detail.
Theorems 2 and 11: outer-arc bound 'poly(n) exp(-c n^{1/3})' and the implicit-function step rely on unstated uniformity over the 6 or 34 residue classes; not verified.
Prop. 12 uses sqrt(n+1)<=sqrt(2n) and (1+an)^K, fine, but q^K<1 and Delta>0 depend on a=1-q^2 with K=ceil(4/a); I only spot-checked.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact limit 1/sqrt8 of the circle-root residual (arbitrary slope and restricted) via Mathieu ground state.
Collapse of the residual with exactly one interior zero (rate n^{-1/6}), giving the exact zero-count threshold.
